frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Culpable guilt-charge: a blameworthy liability that accrues to and is borne by an accountable agent, registering against him as an earned debit that makes him answerable to requital.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Culpable guilt-charge: a blameworthy liability that accrues to and is borne by an accountable agent, registering against him as an earned debit that makes him answerable to requital.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 48 occurrences the root does not name harm done to others or mere error; it names the guilt-debit that an act (or inner state) charges to its doer's own account. The packet's own grammar shows this: ithm is earned (kasaba/iktasaba 4:111, 4:112, 24:11, 6:120), carried (iḥtamala 4:112, 33:58), borne away with (tabūʾa bi-ithmī wa-ithmika 5:29), deserved/incurred (istaḥaqqā ithman 5:107), increased as a balance (li-yazdādū ithman 3:178), and rests "upon" someone or not (fa-lā ithma ʿalayhi 2:173, 2:182, 2:203; ithmuhu ʿalā alladhīna yubaddilūnahu 2:181). It attaches even to purely inner acts (baʿḍu al-ẓanni ithm 49:12; āthimun qalbuhu 2:283; ẓāhir al-ithm wa-bāṭinahu 6:120), confirming that the residue is culpability charged to the person rather than external damage. Objects can contain guilt-generating potential (wine/gambling: fīhimā ithmun kabīr 2:219), whose exact negation is the paradise drink that produces lā taʾthīm (52:23, 56:25). The agent forms name the bearer (āthim 2:283, 5:106, 76:24) and the habitual accumulator (athīm 7x), and athām (25:68) names the moment the accumulated liability falls due.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ROOT residue = culpable guilt-charge accruing to an agent. FORM layer: the bare noun ithm names the charge itself; faʿāl pattern athām (25:68) names the outcome/payment side of the same charge; active participle āthim names the current bearer; intensive faʿīl athīm names the habitual accumulator; Form II verbal noun taʾthīm (52:23, 56:25) adds causation/imputation — making or declaring guilty. CONSTRUCTION layer: ʿalā-phrases mark attachment/non-attachment of the charge; bi- phrases mark it as instrument/content of collusion (2:85, 58:8-9); kasaba/iḥtamala/bāʾa/istaḥaqqa mark acquisition and bearing. CONTEXT layer supplies the domain (testimony 2:283, 5:106-107; inheritance 2:181-182; food law 2:173, 5:3; pilgrimage timing 2:203; speech 5:63; suspicion 49:12) without altering the residue.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 25:68 "wa-man yafʿal dhālika yalqa athāman" — here the word denotes the penal consequence met, not the wrongful charge itself, so the residue is not an act-description at all. It reconciles only after a pattern-layer subtraction: faʿāl as outcome-noun, the guilt-debit falling due ("meets" fits a consequence, not an act). Secondary candidate: 2:219 predicates ithm of objects (wine and gambling contain "great ithm"), where no agent is on stage; resolved as the guilt-liability the things generate for their users, supported internally by the paradise-wine mirror "lā taʾthīm" (52:23, 56:25).
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: That ʾ-ṯ-m is simply a generic synonym of "sin/wrong act" (like dhanb or sayyiʾah). Rejected as less precise on internal evidence: (1) the systematic acquisitional grammar (kasaba, iḥtamala, bāʾa bi-, istaḥaqqa, ʿalā) treats ithm as a chargeable debit, not just a deed; (2) 4:112 explicitly disjoins khaṭīʾah OR ithm, so ithm is not coextensive with wrongdoing generally; (3) ithm applies to inner states with no outward deed (49:12, 2:283); (4) athām as requital derives naturally from "liability falling due" but awkwardly from "wrong act."
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from its most frequent packet-internal partners: ʿudwān (paired 5x: 2:85, 5:2, 5:62, 58:8, 58:9) is other-directed aggression while ithm is the self-accruing guilt-charge — the pairing covers inward debit plus outward transgression; buhtān (paired 3x: 4:20, 4:112, 33:58) is falsehood thrown at another, while the ithm of the same act accrues to the thrower; fawāḥish (42:37, 53:32, 7:33) are flagrant excesses subsumed under or set beside kabāʾir al-ithm, the broader liability category; khaṭīʾah (4:112) can be a slip, ithm is the culpable charge. Falsifiable: the hypothesis fails if any occurrence used the root for harm or wrong with no conceivable accountability-debit on an agent (e.g., of natural damage or a non-accountable actor); none of the 48 does.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 48 confirmed occurrences were individually assessed and every one exhibits the proposed residue (culpable guilt-charge accruing to an agent) after subtracting form, construction, and context. The evidence is unusually convergent: the acquisition/attachment grammar recurs across independent suras and genres (law, narrative, eschatology), the participle and intensive forms name bearers of exactly this charge, and the two Form II occurrences plus 2:219 form a coherent internal wine/guilt system (worldly wine contains ithm; paradise wine causes no taʾthīm). The only occurrence requiring nontrivial work, 25:68 athām, resolves cleanly at the pattern layer as the liability's requital and does not require importing external evidence. No occurrence had to be forced, so universal presence holds with no unresolved cases.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Packet: D:\APP	afseer\lisanapp3\data\campaign\packets atch04\Avm.json (48 occurrences, full_coverage=true). The proposed contribution bundles a robust core (culpable/blameworthy guilt) with over-specified machinery (accrues to/borne by an accountable agent as an EARNED DEBIT answerable to requital). The core is universal; the machinery is NOT demonstrably present in every occurrence, so universal presence of the STATED contribution fails.

Strong-fit cluster (machinery genuinely present): 4:111 (yaksib ithman... yaksibuhu ala nafsihi), 24:11 (ma iktasaba min al-ithm), 6:120 (yaksibuna l-ithma sa-yujzawn), 3:178 (li-yazdadu ithman), 5:107 (istahaqqa ithman), 5:29 (tabu'a bi-ithmi), 2:181 (ithmuhu ala...), 4:112/4:20/33:58 (ihtamala + bahtan + ithman mubinan), 2:283 (athimun qalbuh), 5:106 (al-athimin). ADJ forms (26:222, 2:276, 44:44, 45:7, 4:107, 68:12, 83:12) describe the accountable agent bearing guilt. Negated 'fa-la ithma alayhi' (2:173, 2:203 x2, 2:182:11) are RECONCILABLE — negation presupposes the charge-upon-agent structure.

Failing occurrences (machinery absent after allowing form/construction/context):
- 2:219 (both tokens): ithm as harm-quantum inhering IN objects (khamr/maysir), weighed vs manafi (benefit); not an agent-borne earned debit. Clearest refutation.
- 25:68 (yalqa athama): denotes the penalty/requital encountered, not the borne guilt-charge; directionality inverted vs component (d).
- 2:188 (bil-ithm): instrumental 'by wrongful means'; ithm = wrongful manner, not a debit registering against the agent.
- 52:23 & 56:25 (Form II ta'thim): predicated of Paradise's cups as an ABSENT property; even allowing Form II causation, agent-borne-debit/requital is absent.
- 2:182:7 (weaker): ithm = deliberate wrongful bias feared in a bequest (paired with janaf) — an objective fault; machinery backgrounded. 49:12 (predicative 'ba'da l-zanni ithm') similarly backgrounds it.

Distinctiveness (false): after subtracting the constructions (kasaba/iktasaba 'earn', ihtamala 'bear', istahaqqa 'merit', ala 'upon'), the root residue is just 'culpable guilt', which does not separate Avm from dhanb/jurm/zulm — the earning/bearing flavor is imported from those verbs, not the root. Within-packet ithm is distinguished from khati'a (4:112) and udwan (al-ithm wal-udwan: 2:85, 5:2, 5:62, 58:8, 58:9), but the proposed gloss does not capture that contrast.

Falsifiable (true): the claim predicts ithm is always an agent-borne debit answerable to requital; 2:219 falsifies this. Under non-negotiable root unity, universal presence of the stated contribution does not hold (verdict != SUPPORTED); a weaker 'culpable/blameworthy guilt' residue holds across all 48 occurrences.

occurrence_dispositions.note: athAm names the accumulated guilt-liability falling due as requital (yalqa athAman); requital-answerability is explicitly within the frozen contribution, and the guilt-charge is its substance.
Guilt-generating potential located 'in' wine/gambling (fIhimA ithmun kabIr) is the guilt-charge that accrues to the user; the debit-to-agent sense is present as the source of that liability.
ta'thIm (form II) = guilt-inducing/charging; its negation for the paradise cup (lA ... ta'thIm) is the exact negation of the guilt-charge, so the root contribution is present as what is denied.
Same as 52:23 — negated ta'thIm; the guilt-charge is present as the denied liability of the paradise drink.
